prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

UKIP Manifesto 2015 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core stance
- Leave the EU to restore sovereignty, control borders, cut costs, and strike UK-led trade deals. Hold an early in/out referendum (British citizens only), prefer Article 50 with a two-year exit plan. Create a Post‑EU Secretariat to manage withdrawal, review EU law, and rejoin the WTO as an independent member.

Fiscal plan and funding
- Independently costed (Cebr). Fund priorities by: leaving the EU (save ~£9bn net/yr), cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system, ending “health tourism,” and cutting government/quangos/Westminster costs.
- Enable investment without raising taxes or debt: +£12bn NHS over 5 years; +£5.2bn social care; more police, prison and Border staff; defence to ≥2% of GDP; carers +£572/yr; mental health and dementia funding uplift; housing and veterans’ measures.

Tax and economy
- Raise personal allowance to at least £13,000; take minimum wage out of income tax. Raise 40% threshold to £55,000; introduce 30% band (between £43,500–£55,000). Abolish Inheritance Tax. Increase transferable allowance for married couples/civil partners to £1,500. Long‑term aim: 20/30/40% bands.
- Tackle multinational tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.
- Cut small business rates by 20% up to £50,000 RV; crack down on late payments (HMRC enforcement); pilot trade credit insurance; reduce EU red tape; open public contracts to SMEs.

Immigration and borders
- Take back control; five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; Australian‑style points system capped at 50,000 high‑skill visas; equal rules for all nations; count in/out; +2,500 Border Agency staff; no amnesty for illegals; fast-track deportation of foreign criminals.
- Five‑year prior contribution for access to benefits and non‑urgent NHS; students and visitors need insurance. EU citizens resident at referendum can stay and apply for citizenship after five years.

NHS and social care
- Extra £3bn/yr by end of parliament; 8,000 more GPs; 20,000 nurses; 3,000 midwives; free hospital parking; tackle “health tourism”; exclude NHS from TTIP; scrap PFI use; replace CQC/Monitor with elected county health boards; “Licence to Manage” for NHS managers; scrap EU Working Time and Clinical Trials directives.
- Social care: integrate with NHS; restore funding to 2010 levels (+£1.2bn/yr by year 3); Dignity Code; end 15‑minute visits; improve carers’ support; consider fracking‑funded Sovereign Wealth Fund for care cap.

Welfare, pensions, family
- Lower benefit cap; stop welfare tourism (five‑year ban for migrants); limit Child Benefit to two children for new claims; stop Child Benefit paid abroad; scrap Bedroom Tax; keep HB for under‑25s; GP‑led disability assessments; support foodbanks with trained advisers.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions advice; criminalise pension cold‑calling; lifelong war widows’ pensions.
- Childcare: deregulate to expand affordable places (with basic safeguards); wrap‑around care 8am–6pm in primaries; emergency childcare register; foster/adoption sped up; shared parenting presumption.

Education
- Abolish KS1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; secondary choice including grammar, technical and vocational routes; later transfer tests; restore Intermediate GCSE maths tier; remove AS as stepping stone; first aid in PSHE; reverse special school closures; refocus Ofsted.
- Waive tuition fees for UK students in STEMM/medicine who work and pay tax in UK for 5 years; stop loans to EEA students post‑EU exit.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield (national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief up to £250k first sale); bring empty homes back; build up to 1m brownfield homes by 2025; protect green belt and prime farmland; local referenda on large developments; social housing priority for locals; no social housing for foreigners until five years’ contributions; reinvest 100% Right to Buy receipts; no mansion tax; make mortgages inheritable.

Energy and transport
- Repeal Climate Change Act; end subsidies for new wind/solar; back diverse mix (nuclear, gas, coal, hydro); support shale with strict safeguards and a Sovereign Wealth Fund; scrap green levies and EU ETS; fairer billing (end prepay penalties).
- Scrap HS2; consider re‑opening Manston Airport; restrict speed cameras to safety use; end road tolls; oppose EU eCall tracking; scrap DCPC; double HGV levy on foreign trucks; VED exemption for 25+ year vehicles.

Crime, justice and defence
- Leave ECHR and repeal HRA; UK Bill of Rights; scrap European Arrest Warrant; more frontline police/prison/border staff; rationalise constabularies; tough on online/cyber, exploitation, trafficking; cut FOBT max stake to £2; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment.
- Prisons: maintain capacity; deport foreign prisoners; education and victim compensation; no prisoner votes.
- Defence: raise spending to ≥2% GDP (then higher); restore capabilities; retain Trident; cautious on carriers/F‑35; create Director of National Intelligence; no EU army; no income tax on active overseas service; dedicated military hospital.

Agriculture, fishing, heritage, culture, trade
- New UK farm payments focused on small/family farms; fair dairy chain; stronger animal welfare; honest food labelling; support small abattoirs; ban live exports.
- Leave CFP; 12‑mile coastal and 200‑mile EEZ; rebuild stocks; back under‑10m boats; protect sea angling.
- Heritage/tourism: Minister for Heritage; zero‑rate VAT on listed repairs; conservation presumption; seaside town regeneration; save pubs (support microbreweries; optional smoking rooms; oppose minimum pricing).
- British culture: promote integration and English language; protect free speech; uphold one law for all; mandatory FGM reporting; St George’s/St David’s Day bank holidays.
- Trade: bespoke UK‑EU free‑trade deal post‑Brexit; global FTAs via WTO; rebut “3m jobs lost” myth.

Political and local reform
- Citizens’ Initiative referendums; robust Right of Recall (20% trigger); open primaries option; select committee confirmation and spending veto powers; proportional voting with constituency link; restrict GE voting to British citizens (and reciprocal cases); overhaul postal voting; strengthen local referenda, cut council waste, restore weekly bins, zero tolerance on ASB and illegal traveller sites.
